abstract: In anticipation of future digital broadcasting, we have evaluated digital video compression schemes to determine which would be most suitable for the storage and transmission of contribution television program material.1 Various digital compression devices for transmitting and storing video images have been researched and developed, and some are now being applied to broadcasting applications. In evaluating their picture quality, no problems were encountered when using a single device; however, when connecting several compression devices in a cascaded sequence, picture quality deteriorated. The application of digital video-compression techniques to digital-broadcasting distribution and transmission was investigated. This paper describes important factors that determine video quality in cascaded compression systems. It interprets the requirements placed on compression techniques in transmission and post-production and concludes by examining results from several cascaded compression experiments using MPEG-2, Motion JPEG, etc.

authors.bio: Tadayuki Uchida received a B.S. degree in electronic engineering from the University of Tokyo, Japan, in 1981. That year he joined Nippon Hoso Kyokai (NHK, Japan Broadcasting Corp.), and from 1989 to 1995 was with the Technical Planning Division of NHK Engineering Headquarters in Tokyo, working on investment planning of the facilities including HDTV. —In 1995, Uchida was with the Engineering Development Center, involved in developing broadcasting equipment. In 1998, he joined the Planning and General Affairs Division of NHK Hiroshima Regional Head-quarters, working on technical planning and development of local stations' facilities.
authors.name: Tadayuki Uchida

authors.bio: Yasuaki Nishida received the B.S. degree in materials science from the University of Electro-Communications, Tokyo, Japan, in 1973. That year he joined Nippon Hoso Kyokai (NHK, Japan Broadcasting Corp.), and from 1973 to 1977 was with NHK Ohsaka Regional Headquarters. In 1977, he joined NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories, working on video recording and solid-state (MNOS disc memories), and later was engaged in the development of solid-state image sensors as a senior scientist. Since 1995, he has been in charge of research activities in picture quality and digital trans- mission systems for the Engineering Developing Center of NHK Engineering Headquarters in Tokyo. — Nishida is the chairman of R&D Group for the Program Material Transmission Systems in ARIB, and a member of IEEE, ITE, and IEICE.
authors.name: Yasuaki Nishida

authors.bio: Yukihiro Nishida graduated from Keio University with a BSEE in 1983 and with an MSEE in 1985. He joined NHK (Japan Broadcasting Corp.) in 1985. Since 1988 he has been with NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories in charge of research and development on coding and transmission for digital television systems and their performance evaluation. In 1992, he was a visiting engineer at the RAI Research Center in Turin, Italy. — Nishida serves on standardization committees in the area of studio standards and video coding. He is a member of IEICE and ITE of Japan.
authors.name: Yukihiro Nishida
